headline: 5 Reasonable Edit Requests Publishing Houses Are Now Sending To Aspiring Authors
body:
1. Replacing all instances of 'The sun rose' with a 400-page historical backgrounder on the solar system to ensure complete reader context.

2. Mandatory insertion of a disclaimer on the copyright page stating that all fictional characters are actually currently undergoing therapy for their unrealistic plot arcs.

3. Changing the book's climax from a dramatic confrontation to a three-chapter administrative committee meeting to better reflect the modern bureaucratic experience.

4. Requiring the author to provide an end-of-chapter 'Vibe Check' scorecard that allows readers to decide if the plot development aligns with their personal aesthetic preferences.

5. Adding a mandatory appendix that includes a 5,000-word apology note to every hypothetical reader who might feel slightly confused, mildly inconvenienced, or accidentally enlightened by the narrative.
caption: Publishing is all about 'collaboration', right? If you've ever had to edit your life story to suit a boardroom's taste, this one is for you. #BookTwitter #WritingCommunity #PublishingLife (satire)
igHook: Tag an author who has definitely been asked to change their ending to a board meeting.
imagePrompt: A cluttered, dimly lit wooden desk featuring a single manuscript page covered in an excessive number of bright neon sticky notes and red ink markings.

sourceHeadline.title: Penguin India won’t publish Sonia Gandhi’s book, had asked for ‘changes’ which author rejected

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 balances the specific anxieties of the publishing industry with a charmingly absurd, deadpan delivery. It avoids the 'classic literature rewrite' trope seen in many other entries (which feels a bit overdone) and provides fresh, imaginative editorial demands that resonate with the modern writing experience.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article is a harmless, lighthearted satire about the publishing industry that does not target real individuals, groups, or sensitive topics. The image prompt is generic and does not violate any content policies.
